definitions.explanation: Describing people who get along well and have a warm, close relationship. A colloquial i-adjective related to the noun {仲良|なかよ}し.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}はとても{仲良|なかよ}い。
examples.english: The two of them are very close.

examples.japanese: {兄弟|きょうだい}が{仲良|なかよ}いのはいいことだ。
examples.english: It's a good thing when siblings are on good terms.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}とは{学生|がくせい}{時代|じだい}からずっと{仲良|なかよ}くしている。
examples.english: I've been on good terms with her ever since our student days.

notes:
A colloquial i-adjective meaning that people get along well. Built from {仲|なか} (relationship) + {良|よ}い (good).

USAGE:
- The more standard ways to say this are {仲|なか}がいい / {仲|なか}がよい (with が) and the set phrase {仲|なか}のいい. {仲良|なかよ}い as a single word is common in casual speech and writing.
- The adverbial {仲良|なかよ}く is very common: {仲良|なかよ}くする (to get along), {仲良|なかよ}くなる (to become friends).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {仲良|なかよ}し: a close friend; being close — the noun form, also used as a na-adjective
- {親|した}しい: close, intimate — emphasizes depth of a personal bond rather than simply getting along
